title: Check whether a service starts at boot
summary: Ask systemd whether a specific service is enabled to start automatically when the computer boots. These commands only read information and change nothing.

aliases.text: check if service starts on boot linux
проверить включен ли сервис при старте

prerequisites: A Linux system that uses systemd (most desktop distributions do)
The exact service name, or a word from it, such as ssh or cups

steps.explain: List the system services with their boot state. Look for your service in the first column, UNIT FILE, which ends in .service. The STATE column shows whether it starts at boot.
steps.expect: A table with columns UNIT FILE, STATE and PRESET. STATE is typically enabled, disabled, static or masked. Press q to quit if the list is long.

alternatives.explain: Run the command with the name of the service (unit) you want to check. It will print 'enabled', 'disabled', or other states.

placeholders.name: UNIT
placeholders.description: The name of the service or unit file to check, e.g., sshd.service or bluetooth.service.

steps.explain: Ask systemd directly about one service. The answer is printed on one line and is the boot state of that service.
steps.expect: enabled: starts at every boot. disabled: does not start at boot. static: started only by other services. masked: blocked. enabled-runtime: starts until the next reboot only.

alternatives.explain: Show the full status of the service. In the Loaded line, enabled or disabled shows the boot state, and the Active line shows whether it is running now. Press q to quit.
alternatives.expect: A Loaded: line such as loaded (/usr/lib/systemd/system/ssh.service; enabled; preset: enabled), followed by the Active: line.

alternatives.explain: Show every service that is enabled to start at boot, to see them all at once.
alternatives.expect: Only services whose STATE is enabled. If your service is not in this list, it does not start at boot.
